brief:
Shehab Wire examines how Britain's administration of Palestine in the early twentieth century transformed what was framed as a sacred trust into an extended disaster. Official Palestinian government documents from the first half of the 1900s bore the British royal coat of arms—the crowned lion and unicorn—marking Britain's formal authority over the territory following World War I.

Researchers analyzing contemporary historical records point to the contradiction between Britain's stated mandate obligations and the consequences that unfolded across Palestinian society during the period of British governance. The documents themselves, bearing symbols of British sovereignty, stand as physical evidence of the administrative apparatus that oversaw transformations in Palestinian territory and demographics during this era.
